jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Saint Lucia has no AI law, strategy or guidance of its own. Its only AI-relevant instrument is the Data Protection Act 2011, which is only partly in force; its section giving people the right to know the logic of automated processing has not yet commenced. In 2026 the Ministry of the Public Service sought a consultancy, funded by the World Bank, to draft the country's first AI policy and legislative framework.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the Attorney General's Chambers' online laws and government websites. The Saint Lucia Gazette has no online keyword search and Parliament's bills list was not checked directly. The planned AI policy and legislation are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: Data Protection Act (Act 11 of 2011, as amended by Act 2 of 2015)
instruments.publisher_name: Attorney General's Chambers of Saint Lucia (Revised Laws of Saint Lucia, 2023)
instruments.summary: Saint Lucia's general data protection law: it applies to data controllers established in Saint Lucia or using equipment there, binds the State, sets Data Protection Principles (Schedule 2) and rules on consent, sensitive data, accuracy, security, destruction and cross-border transfer, and creates a Data Protection Commissioner with investigation, enforcement-notice and (from the 2015 amendment, s. 12A) privacy-impact-assessment powers over government departments. Section 52 gives data subjects a right to be told the logic involved in any automatic processing of their personal data, the Act's only provision aimed at automated decision-making; it contains no AI-specific rules.
instruments.current_status: Only partly in force: the Revised Laws (2023) note states Act 11 of 2011 is in force from 31 January 2023 for Part I, sections 32 to 43 of Part III, Part VI and paragraphs (a) to (g) of Schedule 2 (S.I. 4/2023); amending Act 2 of 2015 in force 13 April 2015. Part II (Data Protection Commissioner), sections 44-45, Part IV (registration), Part V (data subject rights, incl. the s. 52 automatic-processing logic right) and Part VII are not listed as commenced. Section 1 (as substituted in 2015) lets the Minister commence different Parts by Gazette order. Only the year of enactment (2011) is stated on the official page.
instruments.scope: Processing of personal data by data controllers in Saint Lucia, public and private sector
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Revised Laws of Saint Lucia (2023) pages on attorneygeneralchambers.com read: Act front page (commencement note, arrangement of sections), ss. 1, 3, 12A, 32, 52 and subsidiary-legislation page (none listed).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that governs AI training and use on personal data; s. 52 automatic-processing logic right (not yet commenced).
